Summary of what I saved (skill, not memory, since memory is full):

The error was a small +0.38% systematic overstatement (4984.6 vs 4965.8), which is the signature of including one extra small component in an "all series" total — not a random transcription slip. I added a "SALES, ALL-SERIES COMBINED, CALENDAR-YEAR TOTAL, multi-year MEAN" section to the savings-bonds reference covering:

- Scope trap: "all series combined" = savings BONDS only (E, F, G, H, J, K); EXCLUDE U.S. Savings Notes / Treasury Savings Notes / exchanges. Adding the small Savings-Notes or J/K line is exactly a ~0.4% overstatement.
- Sales vs exchanges: when F&G were discontinued (1952) holders exchanged into H/J/K; use plain gross cash SALES, not "sales including exchanges."
- Calendar-year vs fiscal-year row selection (Q said calendar 1949-1953).
- Use the printed all-series Total line, don't hand-sum components.
- Back-solve target: gold 4965.8 ⇒ 5-year sum 24829.0 M; my ~24924 had ~95M extra to drop.

Also updated the SKILL.md pointer so this reference is surfaced for sales/calendar-year-mean questions, not just redemption-share ones.
